findings.message: `AdbcHook` already names these two values separately - `conn_name_attr = "adbc_conn_id"` and `default_conn_name = "adbc_default"` - and restating the literal here (and again at line 269 in `AdbcHookWithRealGetConn`) has collapsed them: the mock sets `conn_name_attr` to the *default conn id*, so the subclass under test no longer accepts `adbc_conn_id=` at all and only works by accident. Drop the override and let the mock inherit `AdbcHook.conn_name_attr`; likewise build the `Connection(...)` fixtures from `AdbcHook.default_conn_name` / `AdbcHook.conn_type` rather than repeating "adbc_default"/"adbc" in six places.

`_driver_path` is added here with four outcomes - the wheel-bundled `lib<driver>.so`, the `sys.prefix/lib` `.so`/`.dylib` pair, the Conda-on-Windows `.dll`, and the bare-`self.driver` fallback - and no test takes any of them: every `get_conn` test stubs it out with `hook.__dict__["_driver_path"] = "adbc_driver_sqlite"`, and `test_dbapi_connection` is skipped unless `adbc_driver_sqlite` is installed and asserts nothing about the resolved path. Add cases that fake each lookup (patch `importlib_resources.files` / `pathlib.Path.is_file`) and assert the path chosen, including the fallback.

Only the `"::" in host` side of this conditional is exercised - every test connection uses `host="file::memory:"` - so the else branch that calls `get_uri()` and rewrites the `adbc://` scheme to the dialect name never runs, even though docs/connections/adbc.rst documents it as the login/password path (`<dialect>://login:password@host/schema`). Add a `uri` test with a plain host plus login/password and `dialect: postgresql`, asserting the scheme is rewritten.

`ENV_ID` is added here and no task, id or resource name in this Dag reads it - `DAG_ID` and `CONN_ID` are both fixed strings. Either fold it into the identifiers the system test creates (as the other system-test Dags do) or drop the constant and the `os` import.
